name: Toadstool Geologic Park Surrounding Free Primitive Camping - Ogallala Grassland

management_agency.name: U.S. Forest Service - Pine Ridge Job Corps / Pine Ridge Ranger District

rules_and_regulations.cost: 100% Free - No fees, no permits required for general grassland dispersed camping outside developed campground
rules_and_regulations.stay_limit: 14 consecutive days max stay within 30-day period
rules_and_regulations.guidelines: Dispersed primitive camping permitted on general Ogallala National Grassland public lands. Must park within 30ft of public forest roads. Driving off-road prohibited.

waste_disposal_rules.poop_disposal: Cathole method: dig 6 inches deep in clay badlands soil, 200 feet from dry washes. Pack out toilet paper.
waste_disposal_rules.trash_policy: Strict Leave No Trace pack-it-in pack-it-out.

campfire_rules.firewood_policy: Bring your own firewood; prairie badlands wood gathering non-existent.
campfire_rules.safety_requirements: Campfires in containerized fire pans or existing rock rings only due to extreme prairie grass fire hazard. Extinguish cold to touch.
campfire_rules.seasonal_fire_bans: Obey Red Flag Warning fire bans.

access_and_road_conditions.road_type: Unpaved gravel and dirt prairie road (Toadstool Road / FS 904)
access_and_road_conditions.road_conditions: Washboard gravel road crossing clay badlands. Can turn slick and impassable wet gumbo clay after heavy rain.
access_and_road_conditions.vehicle_recommendation: Normal low clearance front wheel drive car (accessible along Toadstool Road in dry conditions; high clearance recommended for remote spurs)

nomad_connectivity_rating.terrain_obstruction_risk: Low (Unobstructed high prairie horizon with volcanic badland formations)

seasonal_weather_effects.spring: 55-70°F, high winds, spring rain turning clay roads to gumbo mud.
seasonal_weather_effects.summer: Hot (88-98°F), intense solar heat, afternoon severe lightning thunderstorms.
seasonal_weather_effects.fall: Ideal prairie boondocking season (60-75°F daytime, 35-45°F nights), dry clear skies.
seasonal_weather_effects.winter: Cold High Plains winter (20-40°F daytime, sub-zero nights), heavy blowing snow.

dangers_and_hazards: Prairie wildfires during dry Red Flag Warnings
Gumbo clay roads becoming impassable when wet
Prairie Rattlesnakes active in summer months

common_human_made_sounds: Infrequent visitor car on Toadstool Road
Wind blowing over ancient badland rock formations

common_animals: Bighorn Sheep (reintroduced in nearby Pine Ridge)

human_demographics_and_culture: Paleontologists and fossil enthusiasts, solar digital nomads, astrophotographers, and overlanders.

spiritual_and_folklore_data.nature_spirits_and_mythological_lore: Lakota Oglala Sioux indigenous traditions revere the Pine Ridge and badlands of northwestern Nebraska as sacred ancestral hunting grounds and spirit vision sites.
spiritual_and_folklore_data.energetic_and_spiritual_features: Ancient Oligocene fossil layer energy, profound stillness, world-class dark skies.

nearby_hiking_trails.features: Winding path through 30-million-year-old badland rock formations and fossil beds

public_reviews_summary: Like camping on the moon! Surreal badland formations, complete silence, and good 4G cell signal. Watch weather carefully so clay roads don't turn to mud.
other_data: Bortle Class 1 night sky (pristine dark sky). High solar power panel output.
